name: Year Zero
title: The Flash Drives Left in Concert Bathrooms
claims: Year Zero is an alternate reality game by 42 Entertainment based on the Nine Inch Nails album | 1
42 Entertainment also made the Halo 2 promotional ARG I Love Bees | 1
Album released April 16, 2007 in Europe and the next day worldwide | 1
Game underway since roughly February 12, 2007, expected to last about eighteen months | 1
Billboard report says the album was due in stores April 17 and the campaign began in early February | 2
Fans found highlighted letters on a NIN tour T-shirt spelling "I am trying to believe", added ".com" and found a website | 2
Other 42 Entertainment sites included anotherversionofthetruth.com and churchofplano.com | 2

Errant clicks produced Bureau of Morality emails calling the user "A CONSUMER OF DISSIDENT MATERIAL" with threats of lost citizenship increments, fines, penalties or imprisonment, and "You have choices. Make the RIGHT ones." | 2
The email pointed to thepriceoftreason.net | 2
Within days, the blogosphere was full of anxious fans sharing experiences on message boards | 2
Another T-shirt had a highlighted Cleveland-area phone number playing a snippet of "Survivalism," then No. 2 on the Modern Rock chart | 2
According to one post, a fan allegedly by happenstance found a USB drive in a bathroom stall at the Coliseum in Lisbon, containing an MP3 of "My Violent Heart" | 2
Additional drives were purportedly found in Barcelona ("Me, I'm Not") and Manchester ("In This Twilight") | 2
Billboard's aside said the flash drive was "yes, Reznor's idea" | 2
Fans shared the files online | 2
A posting alleged the RIAA emailed Idolator and other sites demanding removal of the MP3s; an RIAA representative confirmed it, calling it a "seemingly mind-boggling move" | 2
The whole album had not leaked; per a source, the only leaks were ones Reznor approved | 2
A trailer appeared online by late February; near its end an extended arm, "the Presence," appears, and it is on the album cover | 2
Story set in 2022, termed "Year 0" by the US government, after terrorist attacks including on Los Angeles and Seattle; government took emergency powers and absolute control | 1

Government is a Christian fundamentalist theocracy with a Bureau of Morality and the First Evangelical Church of Plano; licenses needed to marry and bear children, revocable for subversion; dissenters disappear at night to detention centers and sanitariums, if not executed | 1

Cedocore distributes Parepin in the water as an "immune booster"; it is a psychoactive drug reducing aggression, affecting memory and instilling credulity toward authority; most people become apathetic and carefree | 1
Side effects including schizophrenia-like behavior and muscle twitches; effective treatment implied only in urban and developed areas, discouraging moves to rural areas | 1

The Presence appears as massive ghostly hands and arms extending from the sky into the ground; early attribution to mass hysteria; later recorded on video and film, grainy and unfocused; those touched report terror and clarity; prevailing opinion is that it represents God or a supernatural force | 1

On February 10, 2022 an official named Doug writes a letter to his unborn daughter, missing her birth in Denver; Presence sightings occur worldwide; the letter ends with the Presence above the Capitol and "the stars are going out like candles" | 1
The Solutions Backwards Initiative, students, professors and computer experts, devise a way to send information back through time using quantum mechanics | 1
The game's websites and music are implied to be information packets sent through wormholes, activated moments after Doug's message | 1
Reznor said "It's not some kind of gimmick to get you to buy a record - it IS the art form", and called the game "a new entertainment form" | 1

A source told Billboard Reznor may see it not as a marketing campaign but a new entertainment form; "the CD booklet come to life"; it would continue 18 months with peaks and valleys; "No one has assembled the full story yet" | 2
Reznor said the concept was partly inspired by his feelings about the Bush administration, and he wanted to write an essay about where the world might be | 1

Storyline borrows from Orwell (surveillance), Huxley (drugs), Bradbury (censorship), Zamyatin (church and state); resembles Philip K. Dick's Faith of Our Fathers (hallucinogens in water, militaristic state, venerated entity in many forms) | 1
In 2008, 42 Entertainment won two Webby Awards and three One Show medals including gold in online gaming | 1
Ann Powers of the Los Angeles Times called it "a total marriage of the pop and gamer aesthetics" | 1
USA Today and Rolling Stone cited fan sites and forums as sources for discoveries | 1
Reznor called the album the soundtrack to "a movie that doesn't exist" | 1
March 2007 Kerrang! Radio reported Reznor was "in talks" about a film; he later preferred television; August 10, 2007 he said they would pitch networks | 1
Progress stalled reportedly because of the writers' strike; in November 2012 it was "in a holding state" for lack of the right writer | 1
In 2017 Reznor said he had put together a "world bible" for a potential HBO and BBC America adaptation; a writer was hired but it fell apart | 1

sources.title: Cryptic Web sites build buzz for Nine Inch Nails - CNN.com
